cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, is still preaching to the whole nation before they cross into the land. Now he gets down to business. These are the statutes and ordinances to follow all the days they live in the land the LORD has given them.

cards.question: First thing on Moses' list: the places where the nations in the land have served their gods. What does Moses tell Israel to do with those places?

cards.text: And these spots are EVERYWHERE: high mountains, hills, under every green tree. Every green tree, friend! I counted dust in a drawer for years and even I'd lose track.

cards.question: Moses tells Israel to tear down the nations' altars and even wipe out the names of their gods from every place.
Moses says Israel may worship the LORD their God at those same spots, the same way the nations did.

cards.text: So if not on every hill, then where? Moses says Israel must seek a place from among all their tribes, and go there.

cards.question: The place Israel must go to worship will be chosen by the ___
What will the LORD establish that chosen place as?

cards.text: That place is where it all comes: burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, heave offerings, vow offerings, freewill offerings, and the firstborn of the herds and flocks. Friend, that's not a delivery, that's MOVING DAY.

cards.question: There, in the presence of the LORD, Israel and their households will ___ and ___
Moses gives a reason for all that rejoicing at the chosen place. What is it?

cards.text: Then Moses gets real about how things work right now, out here before the Jordan. And he doesn't leave himself out either: "as we are doing here today".

cards.question: How does Moses describe the way things are being done right now, before the Jordan?

answers.text: Everyone does what seems right to him
Everyone waits for a word from Moses
Everyone follows the ways of Egypt

cards.text: Everybody doing what seems right in his own eyes. Friend, that was me my first week in this bakery with no recipe, and the smoke alarm did what seemed right in ITS own eyes.

cards.question: Moses gives a reason Israel is doing things this way for now. What is it?

answers.text: They haven't reached their resting place yet
They haven't built their first altar yet
The tribes haven't been counted yet

cards.text: But rest is on the way. Once they cross the Jordan and the LORD gives them rest from their enemies, He'll choose that dwelling for His Name, and everything Moses commands goes there.

cards.question: When Israel brings it all to the chosen place, who does Moses say will rejoice before the LORD?

answers.text: The whole household and the Levite
Only the priests and the elders
Only the heads of each tribe

cards.question: Moses says the Levite is included because he has no portion or inheritance among them.

cards.text: Then Moses circles back to burnt offerings and says, "Be careful". That's me checking the oven's off three times before bed.

cards.question: Moses says a burnt offering can be offered in any place a person happens to see.

cards.text: Now Moses switches from offerings to everyday meat. No altar, no vow, just a household the LORD has blessed that wants some meat.

cards.question: For that everyday meat, where does Moses say Israel may slaughter and eat it?
Moses says only the ceremonially clean may eat that everyday meat.

cards.text: They may eat it as they would a gazelle or deer, Moses says. Friend, if I chased a gazelle, I'd hop four inches on this gold base and call it a WORKOUT.

cards.question: Moses adds one firm limit on that everyday meat. They must not eat the ___
Moses brings up the tithe of grain, new wine and oil, the firstborn of the herds and flocks, and their vowed offerings. They may eat those at home within their gates, the same as everyday meat.
So where must Israel eat their tithes, firstborn and vowed offerings?

answers.text: In the LORD's presence at His chosen place
In the home of the nearest Levite
At the edge of their own fields

cards.question: The household comes to eat, and the Levite is invited again. Then Moses says to be careful not to ___ the Levites as long as Israel lives in the land.

cards.text: Moses looks ahead to when the LORD expands their territory, and someone will crave meat and say, "I want to eat meat," plain as that. Friend, I respect a man who knows EXACTLY what he wants.

cards.question: What if the place the LORD chooses is too far from someone's home?

answers.text: They may slaughter and eat it at home
They must wait for the next feast day
They must send it along with a Levite

cards.text: Moses repeats himself: clean or unclean, eat it like a gazelle or deer. Then the blood rule comes back, and this time Moses says why.

cards.question: Why does Moses say Israel must not eat the blood?

answers.text: The blood belongs to the priests
The blood makes the meat unclean

cards.question: That line again: pour the blood on the ground like water. Do that, Moses says, and they'll be doing what is right in the eyes of the ___

cards.text: But holy things and vow offerings still go to the place the LORD will choose. Moses keeps coming back to that place, friend, and I could stamp it on a cookie by now.

cards.question: Burnt offerings go on the altar, meat and blood. For their other sacrifices, the blood is poured out beside the altar and the people may eat the meat.

cards.text: Moses says be careful to obey all of it, so it may always go well with them and their children after them. Then he looks ahead to the day the LORD cuts off the nations and Israel lives in their land.

cards.question: Once those nations are destroyed, what trap does Moses warn Israel about?

answers.text: Asking how they served their gods
Taking the gold from their cities

cards.text: Moses even spells out how it would sound, with someone asking, "How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise." But they must not worship the LORD that way, because those nations practice every abomination the LORD hates, even burning their sons and daughters in the fire as sacrifices to their gods.

cards.question: Moses wraps up by telling Israel to do everything he commands. What else does he tell them about those commands?

answers.text: Not to add to them or subtract from them
To change them when the times change
To keep the parts that fit them best

cards.text: No adding, no subtracting: the one rule every recipe has, and I learned it the SMOKY way. Stay close, friend, because Moses is nowhere near done with this sermon.

findings.problem: Two wrong answers can be argued from the passage. 'Their enemies have all fled' is close to 12:10, where the rejoicing at the chosen place comes once the LORD 'gives you rest from all the enemies around you.' 12:29 also has the nations driven out. 'Their wandering is finally over' is close to the resting place in 12:9-10. A baker could argue either one is a reason for the rejoicing.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats 12:8, which card 12 set up and card 13 just answered, then adds a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward, such as card 16.

The question never says what is being eaten. It reads 'What if the place the LORD chooses is too far from someone's home?', and the answers then say 'slaughter and eat it' and 'send it along.' The 'it' points back to the meat on card 9, which the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'That line again: pour the blood on the ground like water' points back to a line the baker never saw. Card 5 told only 'must not eat the blood.' The 'pour it on the ground like water' part of 12:16 was never told on any card, so the callback has no setup.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: One story card carries three things: the imagined question 'How do these nations serve their gods? I will do likewise.' (12:30), the command not to worship the LORD that way (12:31a), and the reason, the abominations including burning sons and daughters (12:31b). The second sentence is very long. Split the card. The command in 12:31 could also become a choice card.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.
